summary.intent: Resume interrupted work on the callisto repo: validate and push the merge-conflict resolution on the allow-list branch (#353), then add a docs follow-up to the taken-name PR (#354) pointing the 'check the name' bullet at E322.
summary.outcome: CI passed on the merged #353 branch after rerunning a flaky test, and the resolution was pushed; both PRs were reported mergeable. The #354 branch had main merged in, docs/publishing.md was edited, and full CI, commit and push were run, but the final mergeability check result isn't shown.

repo: Full CI is run via a helper script (ci.sh) and should be run on the merged tree before pushing a conflict resolution.
Branches cut before PR #350 merged lack the 'First publish' section in docs/publishing.md, so main must be merged in before editing that section.
Work happens in a git worktree at .claude/worktrees/smoke-main.

code.finding: The 'check the name' bullet was updated to point at error code E322 on the taken-name branch; this required the 'First publish' section from #350, which exists only after merging main.

workflow: After a branch switch, re-read a file before editing, because the edit fails on stale content.
GitHub takes a few seconds to recompute mergeability after a push, so recheck before concluding a PR is conflicted; UNSTABLE means checks are still running.
A test that fails in the full CI run but passes alone is likely a load-related flake; rerun it in isolation, then rerun the full pipeline.
Scratch files in /tmp (logs, helper scripts) can be cleaned up between sessions, so be ready to recreate them after an interruption.

friction: An API connectivity error (ENOTFOUND) interrupted the session in the middle of the full CI run.
Scratch CI logs and helper scripts were deleted, so the failing test output was lost and ci.sh had to be recreated.
One CI test failed on the merged tree due to a flake under load.
The first docs edit failed because the branch switch left the file stale, and the branch was missing content from #350.
open_items: Confirm that the #354 follow-up push shows as mergeable and that its CI checks finish green.
Both PRs showed UNSTABLE while checks were still running; verify the final check status before merging.
The flaky test that failed only under load wasn't investigated further.
